{{Quote|I have your kyber crystals. Don't ask how I got them. I'm willing to give them back to you if you make me the right offer.|Jalice Andit, to an Imperial spy|<ref name="Unlock" />}}
'''Jalice Andit''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] [[mercenary]] from the [[moon]] [[Jedha]] who lived in [[Jedha City]] with her [[Marriage|husband]], [[Joali Andit]]. The pair were loosely aligned with resistance fighter [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[partisans]] and aided them in their [[Jedha insurgency|fight]] against the [[Galactic Empire]], although the couple cared more about violence and getting [[Galactic Credit Standard|paid]] than Gerrera's ideals.

After Jalice [[Thief|stole]] a crate of [[kyber crystal]]s from a [[Unidentified Clan of the Toribota pilgrim|lost pilgrim]], Gerrera's men took the crate from her. In exchange for several artifacts, Jalice then provided the location of the [[Unidentified Jedha stronghold|stronghold]] where the partisans had taken the crate to an [[Unidentified Imperial spy (Jedha)|Imperial spy]] who was [[Mission on Jedha|searching]] for the [[crystal]]s.

In [[1 BBY]], Jalice stood in the crowds in [[Tythoni Square]] in Jedha City shortly before the partisans [[Battle on Jedha|ambushed]] a group of [[Imperial Military|Imperials]] there. Jedha City was then [[Destruction of Jedha City|destroyed]] by the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] shortly after the ambush.

==Biography==
===Crates and chaos===
{{Quote|I lied to you! I did have the crate, but Gerrera's men outwitted me and took the crate. So, it is with utmost pleasure that I give you this piece of information: Gerrera's men are hiding east of the broken statues. That's where you'll find your crate.|Jalice Andit, to an Imperial spy|<ref name="Unlock" />}}
[[File:JaliceAnditSeated-Unlock.png|thumb|right|300px|Jalice Andit aided the partisans on Jedha.]]
Jalice Andit was a [[human]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> [[Gender|female]]<ref name="Geektionary" /> from the [[moon]] [[Jedha]]<ref name="Geektionary French" /> who [[Marriage|married]] the human [[Joali Andit]] and worked with him as a two-person [[mercenary]] team.<ref name="Dawn" /> Jalice also worked as a [[merchant]], selling [[Scavenger|scavenged]] goods and [[Weapon|arms]].<ref name="Unlock" /> The pair came to Jedha to fight alongside the [[partisans]] led by resistance fighter [[Saw Gerrera]], aiding them in their [[Campaigns of Saw Gerrera's Partisans|fight]] against the Empire for the thrills and [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]].<ref name="HC34" /> The couple lived together in [[Jedha City]] on the moon during its occupation by the [[Galactic Empire]] and took full advantage of the permanent chaos that prevailed there.<ref name="Geektionary" /> Only loosely aligned with the partisans, they aided them in the [[city]] so long as they were allowed to participate in any outbreaks of [[Jedha insurgency|violence]] and kept getting paid.<ref name="ROUVG" />

Jalice at one point [[Thief|stole]] a crate of [[kyber crystal]]s from a [[Unidentified Clan of the Toribota pilgrim|lost pilgrim]] associated with the [[Clan of the Toribota]]; however, she was then outwitted by Gerrera's men, and they took the crate from her. The [[crystal]]s had originally belonged to the Empire, and an [[Unidentified Imperial spy (Jedha)|Imperial spy]] was [[Mission on Jedha|sent]] to Jedha to retrieve them. The [[spy]] tracked down the [[pilgrim]], who pointed them toward Jalice but warned the Imperial that they would need to give her more than fifty [[Currency|credits]] worth of artifacts in exchange for the crate. Accessing an Imperial dossier that listed Jalice as having suspected past dealings with Gerrera and labeled her as someone to further investigate, the spy used the last known location from the document to find her in the [[Deserted Canyon]], and, after providing her with two ceremonial bowls, some [[pearl]] pilgrim beads, and a pilgrim's ritual pendant that were in total worth fifty-four credits, Jalice revealed that she had lost the crate and instead gave the spy the location of the [[Unidentified Jedha stronghold|stronghold]] where the crate was being held.<ref name="Unlock" />

===In it for the violence===
[[File:JaliceAndit-Unlock.png|thumb|left|300px|Jalice Andit was a greedy and profiteering mercenary.]]
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' to [[1 BBY]].</ref> she stood among a crowd of on looking civilians on the edge of Jedha City's<ref name="RO">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> [[Tythoni Square]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> as other partisans prepared to [[Battle on Jedha|ambush]] an incoming [[Imperial Hammers Elite Armor Unit|group]] of Imperials from the surrounding buildings. Once a group of Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s and a [[TX-225 GAVw "Occupier" combat assault tank]] had entered the square, the partisans attacked, and the crowd Jalice had been standing in fled.<ref name="RO" />

The partisans managed to successfully take out the [[Imperial Army|Imperial forces]] and stole several containers of kyber crystals from the [[TX-225 Occupier|tank]] before fleeing from incoming Imperial reinforcements. Soon after the ambush, the Empire [[Destruction of Jedha City|destroyed]] Jedha City and the partisan base at<ref name="RO" /> the [[Catacombs of Cadera]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> entirely using the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]].<ref name="RO" /> Some partisans on the moon successfully escaped the attack and survived, although others [[Death|perished]] in the blast.<ref name="SW39">[[Star Wars (2015) 39|''Star Wars'' (2015) 39]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Thank you for saving me! I found a crate of holy crystals during my travels, but it was stolen by Jalice Andit! Jalice is greedy and will only trade if you bring her at least fifty credits worth of goods.|A lost pilgrim, to an Imperial spy|<ref name="Unlock" />}}
[[File:JaliceCasitineTythoniSquare-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|Jalice Andit (bottom left) thrived in the chaos of Jedha City.]]
Jalice and Joali Andit were thrill-seekers and profiteers who thrived in the chaos of Jedha City.<ref name="ROUVG" /> A lost pilgrim she robbed considered her greedy, and an Imperial dossier on Jalice marked her as resourceful.<ref name="Unlock" /> Jalice was known for her courage, but it was her and Joali's passion for violence and openness to bribery that led to them becoming a hired workforce for Gerrera, caring more for his credits than his ideals.<ref name="Geektionary" /> After the Partisans took the kyber crystals from her, she took great pleasure in giving their location to the Empire.<ref name="Unlock" /> Jalice had dark skin, [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s, and black [[hair]].<ref name="ROUVG" />

==Equipment==
Jalice Andit wore a brown [[Jacket|coat]] with a darker brown [[scarf]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> that hid half her face,<ref name="HC34" /> an [[Clothing|outfit]] that matched her husband's clothing and that of a number of others in Jedha City.<ref name="RO" /> She also wore black and yellow [[glove]]s and black [[boot]]s.<ref name="Unlock" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Jalice_Andit.png|thumb|right|300px|Jalice Andit, as seen in a promotional reel for ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'']]
Jalice Andit first appeared in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="RO" /> which was released on [[December 16]], [[2016]].<ref name="SW.com">{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books|author=[[James Floyd|Floyd, James]]|date=2016-12-14}}</ref> Prior to the film's release, the character was revealed in the first teaser trailer for ''Rogue One'',<ref name="Teaser">{{SWYouTube|Wji-BZ0oCwg|ROGUE ONE: A STAR WARS STORY Official Teaser Trailer|date=2016-04-07}}</ref> released on [[April 7]], 2016.<ref name="TeaserRelease">{{SW|url=news/watch-the-rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-teaser-trailer|text=Watch the ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer!|date=2016-04-07}}</ref> The character was first identified in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> and released alongside the film.<ref name="SW.com" />
